title: private-installer: CI/CD artifact signing, SBOM & provenance, release manifest generation
author: Ava Nguyen
description: Add end-to-end CI/CD steps to produce signed artifacts, SBOMs, SLSA provenance, and a release manifest for the private-installer release pipeline. Motivation: customers running Redwood Private require cryptographically verifiable artifacts and provenance for air-gapped installs and compliance audits. This PR introduces cosign-based signing of installer bundles, generation of SPDX SBOMs for installer images and packages, SLSA v1/2 provenance attestation files, and a canonical release manifest JSON that the Private deployment tooling and install UI will consume. Changes include new CI jobs, small helper scripts for packaging/attestation, updates to helm chart packaging for deterministic archives, and documentation/alerting for the signing pipeline. Checklist: - [x] Add cosign signing job to CI and key handling via KMS plugin - [x] Produce SPDX SBOMs from container images and tarballs - [x] Emit SLSA provenance attestations with build metadata - [x] Generate canonical release-manifest.json and upload to release bucket - [x] Add integration tests that validate signatures and manifest schema - [x] Add migration docs for installer consumers

build: generate SPDX SBOMs for container images (Ava Nguyen)

diff_summary: Added new CI workflow 'release-private-installer' to perform build -> sbom -> sign -> manifest upload
Added ci/signing helpers and KMS keywrap integration (cosign + GCP KMS plugin support)
Switch to deterministic tarball ordering in charts/pack.sh to ensure stable signatures
Generate SPDX SBOMs from built images and include SBOM URI in release manifest
Produce SLSA provenance attestations using in-repo provenance generator and attach to release artifacts
review_comments: Diego Martinez: Please ensure the KMS keywrap step does not leak raw key material into logs — use redaction for env vars.
Ava Nguyen: Added log redaction and limited scope for COSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY to the job; CI secrets audited.
Priya Kaur: The SBOM generation step is flaky on the first run due to missing image pull caching; can we add a retry/backoff?
Ava Nguyen: Added retry with exponential backoff and a CI cache for image layers; test run showed stabilization.
Samir Patel: Can the release-manifest schema include a 'compatibility' block that indicates installer supported versions? Consider adding a checksum field for each artifact.
Ava Nguyen: Extended manifest schema to include 'compatibility' and sha256 checksums for all uploaded artifacts; updated tests and docs.
release_notes: Adds CI/CD support for cryptographic signing of private-installer artifacts, SBOM generation (SPDX), SLSA provenance attestations, and a canonical release-manifest used by private installs. Improves auditability and enables air-gapped verification for enterprise customers.
notes_for_ops: Deployers must provision a COSIGN key in supported KMS (GCP KMS or AWS KMS via envelope wrapping). Update CI secrets per ci/signing/README.md. Existing install pipelines are backward-compatible but will prefer signed manifests when available.
user_impact: Low - internal change to release pipeline. Installer consumers benefit from signed artifacts; no downgrade required. Some orgs may need to update CI secrets to support KMS-wrapped cosign keys.
security_considerations: Private keys are never stored in plaintext in CI. Cosign key is wrapped by KMS and only unwrapped in ephemeral job agents. Audit logs of key usage are enabled. SBOMs do not include secrets. We added CI gating to ensure signatures and attestations are validated before uploading.
changelog_entry: CI: private-installer release signing + SBOM + provenance + release manifest (Ava Nguyen)
migration_instructions: If you consume private-installer artifacts programmatically, update your verifier to prefer signed manifests (release-manifest.json) and validate sha256 checksums and cosign signatures. See docs/private-installer/release-notes.md for examples.
testing_summary: Added integration test that builds a sample installer bundle in CI, generates SBOM and provenance, performs cosign verification using wrapped key, and validates the release manifest schema. Tests run in ephemeral GKE agents and passed on the final run.
